title: Route pattern matcher
prompt: Build a CLI reading one JSON object {routes,requests} from stdin: routes is an array of {name,pattern} with unique nonempty string names, requests an array of strings. A pattern starts with "/" and consists of "/"-separated segments: a static segment, a parameter segment :name (name matches [a-z][a-z0-9_]*, parameter names unique within a pattern), or a final wildcard segment *, which must be the last segment. A static segment beginning with a backslash is literal with the backslash removed, so \:x is the static text :x and \* is the static text *. The pattern "/" matches only the root path. Empty segments (such as in //), a pattern not starting with "/", an invalid parameter name, a wildcard that is not last, duplicate parameter names, a pattern with a trailing "/" (other than "/" itself) or any other malformed route or malformed input JSON: exit nonzero, leave stdout empty and write a diagnostic to stderr. For each request: the path is the part before the first "?" (the query part is ignored); a single trailing "/" is ignored unless the path is "/"; the path must start with "/" and have no empty segments, otherwise the result is {"error":"bad_request"}; each path segment is percent-decoded (UTF-8), and malformed percent encoding gives {"error":"bad_request"}; a decoded segment may contain "/". A static segment matches a decoded segment equal to its text, a parameter segment matches any one segment, and the wildcard matches one or more remaining segments. Among all matching routes choose the most specific one: compare routes segment by segment from the left, where static beats parameter and parameter beats wildcard at the first position where they differ; if routes are equal in kind at every position the one listed first wins. The result for a request is {"route":NAME,"params":{...}} where params maps parameter names to their decoded text and "*" to the decoded remaining segments joined with "/", or {"route":null,"params":{}} when nothing matches. Print exactly one JSON object and a newline: {results} with one entry per request in order. Exit 0 on success. No external services are needed.
